content:
STAGE 1 - goal: establish the comparison frame.
READ: the rubric (rubric-2026-10-v1, 7 weighted dimensions) and both finalist specs, plus the shared evidence bundle (6 evidence ids E4-E11 observed, E12/E13 proposed geometry for CURVCELL, E12 for cocond). All three idea blocks carry the identical E1-E11 bundle text; only GEOMETRIC_NECESSITY E12/E13 differ per idea.
OBSERVED: A = cocond-markov-poincare-ot (printed first): replaces the Euclidean argmin in each RQ level with a 3-iteration entropic-OT plan, ground cost = Poincare distance at fixed kappa=-1, plan diffused by one Markov step along the training directed-transition matrix between column-marginal projections, argmax column taken as the code, codebook updated as a Klein/Einstein hyperbolic weighted barycenter of assigned latents; alpha and q claimed "measured, never tuned" but the measurement procedure is only referenced ("see SAFEGUARDS") and not given.
B = CURVCELL-SID: per-code negative curvature kappa[l][k] = (log(1+B[l][k])/((d-1)R))^2 from the effective number of distinct successor code-groups of that cell, applied as d_B(eps,c)/sqrt(kappa) in both the argmin and the commitment term, with 12 cumulative-mean refreshes over the 3000-epoch budget.
REASONING: the decisive separation will be on geometry_necessity and novelty (60% of the weight combined), where A moves the assignment operator itself while B rescales a distance per code.
OPEN: score behavior_evidence, geometry_necessity, novelty, downstream, falsifiability, implementability, exploration_value and pick the head-to-head winner.

STAGE 2 - goal: score the two mechanisms on the two 20% dimensions using the evidence ids.
READ: A's novelty paragraph vs B's novelty paragraph; A's E12 (fixed kappa=-1 Poincare cost + Klein/Einstein barycenter) vs B's E12 (kappa[l][k] rescaling, D = 2*atanh(||(-eps) oplus c||)/sqrt(kappa)).
OBSERVED: (i) GEOMETRY: A's curved object is a genuine op change on two operators (cost kernel inside a Sinkhorn fixed point, and the mean operator on the manifold) with a named matched Euclidean control (Euclidean cost + Euclidean weighted mean). B's curved object is a per-code scalar divisor on an already-monotone distance: d_B(eps,c_k)/s_k has the same argmin family as a matched Euclidean weighted-distance control ||eps-c_k||/s_k, and B itself concedes "curvature-rescaled distances are not a metric" so cells can be non-convex or empty. B is rubric 2 ("a matched Euclidean transform could reproduce"), A is 3-4 (plausibly does something the Euclidean control cannot, argued against the control but cancellations not fully ruled out).
(ii) NOVELTY: A's ledger sentence names geodesic rank matching, fork-angle transport, radial shells, Lorentz cones, tangent-space successor residuals, PER-BRANCH CURVATURE and geodesic prefix losses as already done. B is per-code curvature - a variation on the per-branch curvature already in the ledger -> rubric 2. A's Markov-diffused transport plan is a distinct computation relative to that ledger -> rubric 3-4.
(iii) BEHAVIOUR: A's premise is measured - E11 same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted-null 0.067 on the existing SIDs, with E6 giving the recall plateau (l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363 vs the 0.065 target) and E7 the teacher-forced NLL (T4 9.03 for l1_br vs 1.23 for l1_br_euclid). B's premise needs cell-level content-density-vs-branching, which the bundle never measures - E5 is item-level entropy and E8/E9 are cohort statistics; B's link is therefore inference from E5, not a measured behavioural problem (rubric 2-3).
REASONING: A leads on the two heaviest shared dimensions (geometry, novelty) and on behaviour_evidence; B leads only on implementability, a 10% dimension.
OPEN: fix A's failure risk and the exact statistic it must move.

STAGE 3 - goal: test the remaining dimensions and pick the loser's counter-case honestly.
READ: B's cost/spec (no extra parameters, L*K scalars, +2-4% step time, closed-form, clamp, retained beta) vs A's cost/spec (5-8 MFLOPs, <5% transformer step, 1-2 h on four cards, 3 MB/level, eps-guarded row/col normalisation, STE) and A's stated risks.
OBSERVED: implementability favours B (4-5): fully closed-form, no iterative fixed-point solver, no instability, beta inherited. A is differentiable and numerically guarded and affordable in the frozen budget with remaining risks named, but alpha's measurement rule is referenced and not specified, so A is 4 rather than 5. downstream_mechanism: both are specific (A names the argmax column j*(i), prefix hit-rate of the first two tokens, conditional code entropy and Recall@10 with expected directions; B names Spearman |A_k| vs B_k, level-1 conditional entropy and Recall@10) - A 4-5, B 4. falsifiability: A gives behaviour-off, curvature-off and the unmodified Euclidean RQ-VAE as three controls plus a two-branch falsifier (a rises while c does not = decorative structure; neither rises = signal too sparse) -> 4-5; B gives behaviour-off (unit curvature) and geometry-off plus a Spearman failure criterion, a weaker third control -> 3-4. exploration_value: A 4-5 (a genuinely different mechanism, and a negative is informative either way), B 3-4 (near the measured per-branch-curvature family).
REASONING: weight the totals: geometry and novelty are 40% and A is +1 to +2 on each; behaviour is 20% and A is +1; B's only win is implementability at 10%. A wins.
FAILURE RISK (A): E10 says the train transition graph is thin - 115,582 distinct edges, edge_density 5.3266, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526 over the sampled probe - so B_bt can be near the identity and A degenerates into plain fixed-curvature Sinkhorn; E8 shows the frozen Stage1 vectors only put 0.0822 of canonical pairs in one of K=256 clusters (0.0129 for negatives), so the K=256 prefix budget may cap the hit-rate gain regardless of the plan; and E6's l1_br (0.04671) below l1_br_euclid (0.06207) is direct precedent that behaviour-conditioned SIDs can hurt. Any of these plus Sinkhorn+STE desync giving code collapse would make B's safer, closed-form curvature field the better first run. Also, if B's own premise (cell-level branching heterogeneity) were the real bottleneck rather than the assignment plan, my choice is wrong.
OPEN: none - answer recorded.

STAGE 4 - FINAL ANSWER (complete, stands alone).
WINNER: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
FIRST LISTED: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
ARGUMENT: (1) geometry_necessity (20%) - A alters two curved operators in one block, the Poincare ground cost inside a Sinkhorn fixed point and the Klein/Einstein weighted-barycenter codebook mean, and states its matched Euclidean counterpart (Euclidean cost plus Euclidean weighted mean); B's E12 is a per-code scalar divisor on a monotone distance, d_B(eps,c_k)/sqrt(kappa), whose argmin family a matched Euclidean weighted distance ||eps-c_k||/s_k can reproduce, and B concedes the rescaled distance "is not a metric" so cells can be non-convex or empty (rubric 2).
(2) novelty (20%) - A's own ledger names per-branch curvature among the already-measured mechanisms, which is exactly B's cell-sized curvature field, so B is a routine variation (rubric 2); A moves the assignment plan itself via a Markov-diffused entropic-OT plan, a distinct computation relative to geodesic rank matching, fork-angle transport, radial shells, Lorentz cones, tangent residual and geodesic prefix losses (rubric 3-4).
(3) behaviour_evidence (20%) - A's premise is measured on the bundle: E11 same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted-null 0.067, E6 recall plateau at 0.06207/0.06233/0.06363 against the 0.065 target and E7 T4 NLL 9.03 for l1_br vs 1.23 for l1_br_euclid; B's claim that cells are "sized by content density, not branching" needs cell-level statistics the bundle never measures (E5 is item-level entropy, E8/E9 are cohort statistics), so B rests on inference (rubric 2-3). B's only advantage is implementability (10%): closed form, no iterative solver, beta inherited.
FAILURE RISK: E10's thin transition graph (115,582 distinct edges, edge_density 5.3266, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526) can make B_bt near the identity, degrading A to plain fixed-curvature Sinkhorn; E8's K=256 ceiling (0.0822 shared-cluster share, 0.0129 negative) may cap prefix hit-rate independent of the plan; E6's l1_br 0.04671 < l1_br_euclid 0.06207 is precedent that behaviour-conditioned SIDs can hurt; Sinkhorn plus STE desync can collapse codes, and A never specifies how alpha is measured. If cell-level branching heterogeneity, not the assignment plan, is the binding constraint, B was the better first run.

STAGE: evidence-bundle inventory and rubric mapping (goal: establish what is frozen vs proposed before scoring).
READ: the frozen bundle for both finalists; BEHAVIORAL_EVIDENCE E1-E11 and GEOMETRIC_NECESSITY E12-E13 are byte-identical across cocond-markov-poincare-ot (bc19762831440f87) and CURVCELL-SID (e9e97242e0e9ed08) except the E12/E13 mechanism text.
OBSERVED: E5 successor-entropy quintiles mean H 0.931->3.405 nats, top-1 mass 0.4375->0.0543, support 2.8->44.3; E6 width-20 beam survival recall@10 0.04671..0.06363 (best resample 0.06363), target-SID-in-beams 0.0678..0.0884; E7 per-position NLL shows the geometry-heavy variants lose T1; E8 first-level capacity at K=256 is 0.0822 (negative 0.0129) vs 0.3106 at K=16; E10 transition graph distinct_edges 115582, mean_out_degree 5.4526; E11 same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067.
REASONING: the bundle is a single shared control, so the comparison is decided by fit-to-E5/E6/E8 and by spec quality, not by data differences.
OPEN: audit A's forward pass and B's refresh rule for internal consistency.

STAGE: mechanism audit of cocond-markov-poincare-ot (goal: test implementability, geometry necessity and the level-1 headroom claim).
READ: the idea text steps (1)-(6), CHANGE, HYPOTHESIS, RISKS, plus E8, E11, E6.
OBSERVED: (a) step (5) forwards log_0(c_{j*}) "with a straight-through gradient from r_i" although CHANGE says only the Euclidean argmin is replaced, so the residual hand-off to level l+1 is either code-only (levels 2..L stop carrying item information and the SID alphabet collapses) or simply unspecified; (b) alpha and q are declared "measured, never tuned (see SAFEGUARDS)" but no measurement rule exists in the text; (c) E8 caps first-level cluster sharing at 0.0822 for K=256 while E11 already measures 0.0907 same-first-prefix; (d) the cost line omits the B x B x K diffusion products (3 per level) from its 5-8 MFLOP estimate.
REASONING: A is the more novel computation (plan-level Markov diffusion is not in the earlier-round ledger) but it is not runnable as written and its target level is already at E8's ceiling.
OPEN: does B's spec hold up better on the same tests?

STAGE: mechanism audit of CURVCELL-SID (goal: same implementability/geometry/control test).
READ: the idea text state/refresh/forward/loss, HYPOTHESIS, RISKS, plus E5, E6, E8.
OBSERVED: (a) the Mobius recursion eps = (-c) (+) eps is explicit and s is detached, so there is no gradient channel into the new state; (b) s_new = log(1+B)/((d-1)R) is closed form and E8's K sweep supports cell radius as the prefix lever; (c) the cumulative mean is written ((t-1)s_old + s_new)/t with t taken from the epoch grid {1,2,4,...,2048}, so the epoch-2048 refresh carries weight 1/2048 and the field freezes on the early noisy partition; (d) "geometry-off keeps the behaviour weights" is only coherent if read as Euclidean d/s with the same s, since s = sqrt(kappa) is the sole behaviour channel; (e) B is a per-code refinement of the per-branch-curvature family measured in E6 (0.05500 / 0.05463 / 0.05500 under the Euclidean 0.06207).
REASONING: B is cheaper, fully differentiable-and-guarded in principle, falsifiable with an internal Spearman diagnostic, and aimed at the lever E8 identifies; its defects are one-line index/definition issues rather than a broken forward pass.
OPEN: score both and pick.

STAGE: final pairwise verdict (goal: one winner, rubric-named arguments with evidence ids, named failure risk).
SCORING (rubric-2026-10-v1): cocond-markov-poincare-ot beh3 geo3 nov4 down3 fals3 impl2 expl4 -> 3.15; CURVCELL-SID beh4 geo3 nov3 down4 fals4 impl4 expl3 -> 3.45.
DECISION: winner CURVCELL-SID; printed first was cocond-markov-poincare-ot.
DECISIVE: (1) behaviour_evidence + downstream_mechanism (35%): E8 puts the level-1 K=256 sharing ceiling at 0.0822 (neg 0.0129) against the already-measured 0.0907 first-prefix rate (E11), and E8 says a small K is what width-20 survival depends on; A reorders a 256-cell plan, B changes the effective cell radius, which is that lever, sized by E5's 0.931->3.405 nat branching spread. (2) implementability + geometry_necessity (30%): A's step (5) hands log_0(c_{j*}) to the next level and leaves alpha and q undefined, and it never names a matched Euclidean cost; B's Mobius residual, closed-form s and detachment are specified. (3) falsifiability + novelty (30%): B has behaviour-off, geometry-off and baseline plus a Spearman falsifier that separates encoder absorption from seed noise, while A's own risk list concedes single-seed ambiguity; A is more novel (4 vs 3) but B's geometry-off arm is the Euclidean control E6 already measures at 0.06207.
FAILURE RISK of B: the encoder cancels the detached s field so the argmin never moves, the epoch-indexed cumulative mean freezes the field early, and non-metric cells can empty out; then B sits at baseline even though E8 says the lever is real.
OPEN: none.

CHECK 1 - rubric pass over both finalists against the shared frozen bundle (E1-E13), same rubric-2026-10-v1 weights.
READ: idea A (cocond-markov-poincare-ot, bundle bc19762831440f87) and idea B (CURVCELL-SID, bundle e9e97242e0e9ed08). Both bundles carry the same E4-E11 observations and differ only in E12/E13 (proposed geometry descriptions).
OBSERVED (per dimension, A vs B):
- behavior_evidence: A names a statistic-backed problem - E11 same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 against a permuted null of 0.067, over the existing baseline item_sids, plus E8's measured first-level ceiling (K=256 -> 0.0822 positive vs 0.0129 negative). B leans on E5 (H 0.931->3.405, support 2.8->44.3 across quintiles) to argue branching varies, but never measures that curvature budget is the binding constraint. A 4, B 3.
- geometry_necessity: A's operations (Poincare ground cost inside a Sinkhorn plan; Klein/Einstein closed-form midpoint) have no exact Euclidean equivalent, and A states the matched counterpart (removing curvature changes both the cost kernel and the mean operator). B's rule is argmin_k d_B(eps,c_k)/s_k, i.e. a per-code temperature on a monotone transform; since atanh(rho) ~ rho near the origin, a scaled-Euclidean assignment argmin_k rho_ik/s_k reproduces it to first order - and per-code scalars cannot define a metric at all. A 4, B 3.
- novelty: A does not appear in the ledger (ledger has geodesic rank matching, fork-angle transport, radial shells, Lorentz cones, tangent-space successor residuals, per-branch curvature, geodesic prefix losses - none diffuse the assignment plan). B's per-code curvature from branching is a variation on E12 of SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ (per-prefix-node curvature from branch counts), only re-estimated per code. A 4, B 2.
WHERE: comparisons rest on E5, E6, E7, E8, E11 and the two E12/E13 proposed entries.
REASONING: A's margin comes from novelty + geometry (40% of the weight) with no decisive loss elsewhere except implementability.
OPEN: whether A's diffusion operator is actually well-posed at batch scale - checked next.

CHECK 2 - decisive implementability / downstream audit of each mechanism's actual operator.
READ: A specification step (4) and cost block; B specification (s_new formula, assignment and commitment term) plus both RISKS lists; E10 (distinct_edges 115582, edges 118315, mean_outgoing_degree 5.4526, edge_density 5.3266, sampled users only).
OBSERVED (A): the diffusion P <- (1-alpha)P + alpha*(B_bt @ P) is applied with P of shape B x K (B=1024), so B_bt must be the batch-restricted B x B transition matrix. With mean out-degree 5.45 over the ~24.5k item catalogue, the expected number of transition edges that land inside one 1024-item batch is 1024*5.4526*(1024/24556) ~ 233, i.e. 233 nonzeros in 1,048,576 entries, about 0.022% dense. So for ~99.98% of rows B_bt@P is exactly zero and the mixture collapses to (1-alpha)P before renormalisation: the mechanism degenerates to curved Sinkhorn plus a batch-composition lottery, and A's own cost estimate ("3 sparse BxB products, 5-8 MFLOPs") only holds because it silently assumes this degenerate density. A's RISK list mis-describes the failure mode as "B_bt close to the identity"; it is close to zero, not to the identity.
OBSERVED (B): s_new = log(1+B)/((d-1)R) and score = d_B(eps,c_k)/s_k. Larger branching B -> larger s -> smaller effective cost -> code claims more items, i.e. the high-fan-out cell grows. That is a defensible "give the fan-out prefix more room" reading, but it is the opposite of what the hypothesis needs: growing the cell of the most diffuse successor set merges behaviourally distinct items into that cell, which pushes H(next code | level-0 code) up, not down, and B never derives why the residual levels below then separate eight branches. B's own risk sentence ("drift toward a few very-low-curvature huge cells") also contradicts its own formula, since low branching, not high, produces low s. Sign bookkeeping is unresolved.
WHERE: E10 supports the density arithmetic; the formulas are from the two specifications.
REASONING: A's flaw is a fixable engineering defect (define B_bt over the full catalogue, gather only the sampled rows) that costs implementability credit but leaves the computation novel. B's flaw is a sign/derivation gap in the causal chain that the hypothesis depends on, which costs downstream_mechanism credit.
OPEN: net weighted totals.

CHECK 3 - weighted totals and final decision.
OBSERVED (weighted, rubric-2026-10-v1): A = behavior 4 (.80) + geometry 4 (.80) + novelty 4 (.80) + downstream 4 (.60) + falsifiability 4 (.40) + implementability 3 (.30) + exploration 4 (.20) = 3.90. B = behavior 3 (.60) + geometry 3 (.60) + novelty 2 (.40) + downstream 3 (.45) + falsifiability 4 (.40) + implementability 4 (.40) + exploration 2 (.10) = 2.95.
DECISION: run A (cocond-markov-poincare-ot) first. A is printed first in the prompt, so winner and first-listed coincide; the decision is on mechanism, not position.
WHERE: E5, E6, E7, E8, E10, E11 plus proposed E12/E13.
REASONING: (1) novelty/exploration - E6/E7 show the whole geometry-plus-successor family already measured negative against Euclidean controls (successor_geodesic_coarse 0.0550, v2 0.0546, tangent_successor_residual 0.0550, successor_entropy 0.0512, all below l1_br_euclid 0.0621 and l1_only 0.0623), and B is another curvature term in the argmin, i.e. that same family. A is the one variant that changes which code an item receives rather than adding another geometric penalty, so it is the untried dimension and its negative would be informative. (2) geometry - A's Klein/Einstein barycenter and Poincare Sinkhorn cost have no exact Euclidean counterpart, whereas B's per-code divisor is a per-prototype temperature reproducible to first order by a scaled Euclidean assignment. (3) downstream - A names the assignment change (argmax of the diffused plan sets j*(i) at every level) and a three-way discriminating outcome (prefix hit-rate rising without recall = decorative coupling; neither rising = transition signal too sparse); B's chain has an unresolved sign.
FAILURE RISK OF THE CHOICE: A's batch-restricted B_bt is ~0.022% dense (233 in-batch edges out of 1.05M entries, from E10), so the Markov step is a near-no-op plus batch-sampling noise; if A is coded exactly as specified the run likely lands at the curved-Sinkhorn level, which E6/E7 place around 0.055, below the 0.062 Euclidean control, while the detached-P Einstein barycenter drifts the codebook and the single-seed protocol cannot separate that from seed noise. E8 is a second way to be wrong: at K=256 the measured first-level co-location ceiling is only 0.0822, so re-planning inside 256 codes may be capacity-capped no matter how good the diffusion is.

FINAL ANSWER (complete, stands on its own).
WINNER: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
FIRST LISTED: cocond-markov-poincare-ot
ARGUMENT: (1) Novelty and exploration value, the 20%+5% dimensions where the two are furthest apart. E6 and E7 are a measured negative for the entire curvature-plus-successor family: successor_geodesic_coarse 0.0550, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.0546, tangent_successor_residual 0.0550 and successor_entropy 0.0512 all sit below the Euclidean controls l1_br_euclid 0.0621 and l1_only 0.0623, and E7 shows the same split in per-position NLL (geometric variants at 2.35-2.53 on T1 against 0.00 for l1_br_euclid). CURVCELL-SID is one more curvature term inside the argmin and commitment, sourced from branch counts, which is a routine variation on the per-prefix-node curvature already in the ledger (SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ, E12); its only new element is an EM-style refresh. cocond-markov-poincare-ot instead changes which code an item receives, by diffusing the entropic-OT plan along training transitions, so its negative would still be informative about an untried dimension.
(2) Geometry necessity. A's curvature does real work that cannot be mimicked: a Poincare ground cost inside a Sinkhorn plan plus a closed-form Klein/Einstein weighted barycenter for the codebook, whose matched counterpart is named (removing curvature changes both the cost kernel and the mean operator). B's rule argmin_k d_B(eps,c_k)/s_k is a per-code temperature on a monotone transform of the Mobius chord; since atanh(rho) ~ rho near the origin, a scaled-Euclidean assignment reproduces it to first order, and a set of per-code scalars cannot define a metric at all, so the "curvature field" is a temperature field wearing a geometry name.
(3) Downstream mechanism. A names the assignment change (argmax of the diffused plan determines j*(i) at every level) and a three-way discriminating outcome: prefix hit-rate rising without recall means decorative coupling, neither rising means the transition signal is too sparse at this scale. B's chain has an unresolved sign: s = log(1+B)/((d-1)R) makes high-branching codes claim larger cells, which merges behaviourally distinct items into exactly the diffuse cell and should raise, not lower, H(next code | level-0 code); B's own risk list even worries about "very-low-curvature huge cells", which its own formula cannot produce. B does win implementability (+2-4% step time versus 1-2 extra hours) but that is 10% of the weight against 40% for novelty plus geometry.
FAILURE RISK: A's diffusion operator is specified over the batch, so B_bt is the batch-restricted B x B transition matrix; from E10's mean out-degree 5.45 over ~24.5k items, a 1024-item batch contains only about 233 transition edges (~0.02% density), so the Markov step is nearly a no-op plus batch-composition noise, and the cost estimate only works because it assumes that degenerate density. Coded as written, A likely falls back to curved Sinkhorn, which E6 places near 0.055, below the 0.062 Euclidean control, while the detached-P Einstein barycenter drifts the codebook and the single-seed protocol cannot separate that from seed noise. E8 is the second way to be wrong: the measured first-level co-location ceiling at K=256 is only 0.0822, so re-planning inside 256 codes could be capacity-capped regardless of diffusion quality.
